name: Strait of Hormuz
note: Iran/Oman strait; ~21 million barrels/day of global crude+products transit here. India sources ~40-45% of its crude via this corridor (Gulf suppliers: Iraq, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait).

name: Bab-el-Mandeb / Red Sea
note: Connects Red Sea to Gulf of Aden; alternate route for Gulf crude to reach India via Suez-bound traffic, also relevant for product/LNG flows. Subject to Houthi attack risk since 2023.

name: Strait of Malacca
note: Relevant mainly for India's crude re-export/product trade with East Asia; minor direct import dependency.

name: Cape of Good Hope (alternate route)
note: Not a chokepoint but the standard reroute option when Bab-el-Mandeb/Suez is unsafe. Adds ~10-14 days transit time West Africa/Gulf to India.

name: West Coast India Direct (Gulf-Kandla/Jamnagar/Vadinar)
note: Primary receiving corridor for Gulf crude into India's largest west-coast refineries.
